A1.justification: Both PDFs describe UniEdit-I with the same authors, BLIP3-o backbone, and GEdit-Bench evaluation. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–C are readable and support comparison despite substantial revision.

before.justification: V1 reports original UniEdit-I benchmark scores, schedule and patience-window experiments, and qualitative editing results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V2 reports revised UniEdit-I benchmark results, latent-space comparisons, gain ablations, convergence statistics, and qualitative experiments.

M1.justification: V1 uses a preset piecewise-decayed offset and threshold-plus-patience stopping. V2 replaces these with gain driven by alignment improvement and a new task-completion score, plus periodic joint-score stopping. Corrective retries remain, but Sections 4.3–4.4 substantially change the inference controller.

E1.justification: GEdit-Bench-EN and its 11 editing categories remain. V2 Section 5.2 adds qualitative scenarios involving vague instructions and user-controlled preservation versus semantic-accuracy preferences. Compound editing already appears in v1, so it is not newly added coverage.

E2.justification: The six benchmark comparators remain GPT-4o, Instruct-Pix2Pix, OmniGen, Step1X-Edit, BAGEL, and OmniGen2. V2 adds explicit FlowEdit window comparisons and linear-decay/no-completion-score controls beyond v1's uniform-versus-piecewise schedule comparison.

E3.justification: V2 introduces a 100-sample latent-space comparison using VLM artifact ratings and temporal CLIP-Sim variability, full-set gain controls with dynamic windowing, and convergence-stage measurement. V1 instead documents 200-sample CLIP/cosine curves and a patience sweep. The benchmark metrics, BLIP3-o-8B, 30-step budget, CFG scales, and three-round cap remain.

E4.justification: V1's schedule and patience sensitivity studies are replaced by four gain configurations, latent-space artifact/feedback analysis, and explicit convergence statistics in v2 Tables 2–4. V2 also adds feedback-preference case studies. Appendix B revises its analysis, although Figures 9–12 reuse the earlier trajectory grids under fixed/dynamic-gain labels.

E5.justification: V2 Table 2 newly reports artifact-score means and standard deviations over 100 samples; v1 reports averaged curves without comparable dispersion estimates. Neither version specifies repeated-seed runs, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new reporting does not establish additional independent runs.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces UniEdit-I's G_SC/G_PQ/G_O values of 6.91/6.80/6.64 with 7.16/7.40/7.06 under the revised controller; comparator scores remain unchanged. All 11 appendix category rows change, and v2 adds artifact, gain, convergence, and qualitative results. These are revised-method results, not an unchanged-configuration performance comparison.

T1.justification: V2 Equation 8 introduces a mathematical gain definition combining alignment improvement, a sigmoid, and completion-dependent attenuation. Much of the trajectory mathematics restates v1's construction through Euler updates and explicit FlowEdit preliminaries. Neither version supplies theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The contributions shift from prescribed coarse-to-fine Dynamic Semantic Editing toward configurable feedback control and user agency. V2 additionally claims that high-quality semantic latent spaces are necessary for reliable closed-loop editing. Training-free UEV editing and state-of-the-art GEdit-Bench performance were already claimed in v1.

C2.justification: V2 develops the argument that clean semantic intermediates enable stable feedback and that completion-aware control prevents over- and under-editing. It removes v1's limitation about heuristic parameters requiring manual tuning and asserts tuning-free adaptation in Appendix B. Inherited VLM biases and difficulties editing text remain acknowledged.

D1.justification: V2 specifies feedback every five steps, gain constants of 1.0 and 15, joint stopping thresholds of 0.85 and 0.9, and example completion/artifact-rating prompts. It also expands BLIP3-o's feature-generation and decoding description. These are useful implementation disclosures, but no new code access, hardware, or runtime information is supplied.

R1.justification: FlowEdit changes from a brief related-work citation to the explicitly acknowledged foundation of the editing trajectory and a central comparator. V2 replaces much of the GPT-4o/projector and semantic-vector motivation with representation-autoencoder positioning, adds VAE/FLUX/RAE references, and removes references including StyleCLIP and CLIPVG.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, method, experimental narrative, conclusion, and substantial appendix passages are rewritten. V2 adds a Preliminaries section, separates editing-related-work subsections, and reorganizes the method and experiments around feedback control.

P2.justification: V1's projector diagram and schedule/patience plots are removed. V2 adds trajectory, editing-window, and preference illustrations plus three analysis tables. Appendix comparisons expand, the color-editing example changes, and retained trajectory grids are resized, relocated, or recaptioned. These are substantial display changes beyond numerical updates and renumbering.

improvement.justification: V2 provides a clearer controller specification, stronger FlowEdit attribution, and useful new controls. However, Section 5.3 reverses Table 2's feedback-stability values, and Section 5.4.1 claims best scores and lowest standard deviation despite higher linear-decay PQ and no reported gain-study deviations. Appendix B also relabels retained piecewise-decay images as dynamic-gain evidence without explaining their provenance. These unresolved evidential problems prevent a reliable judgment that the substantial additions improve overall quality.
